names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 12 mai, «Sfântul Mucenic Ioan Valahul».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 12 Μαΐου, «Άγιος Ιωάννης ο Βλάχος», with the rank word and the epithet left off.

Read out of the heading of days.pravoslavie.ru's name link 968, «Иоанн Влах (Валах), Румынский, мч.», with the rank word left off. The calendar gives the epithet twice over in one heading — Влах and, in its own parenthesis, Валах — and adds Румынский after it; the first spelling is stored and the rest is recorded here, which is how `cyprian-martyr-10-may` carries its three spellings. The day's own line declines him «Мч. Иоанна Валаха (1662) (Рум.).» `fk.mjs` on «Иоанн Влах» returned NONE before the write.

death.note: doxologia.ro: «Și astfel, în anul 1662, în a douăsprezecea zi a lunii mai, pururea-fericitul tânăr Ioan a primit din mâna Domnului cununa biruinței.»

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 12 мая ст. ст. — «Мч. Иоанна Валаха (1662) (Рум.).»

attestations.note: The same menologion day the folder already keeps for the Romanian and the Greek, the same year, 1662, and the same man: the Russian calendar marks him «(Рум.)», a saint of the Romanian church, which is how this source flags an entry it keeps from another local church. **There is no life page behind the line** — the entry is the line and a name link, 968, headed «Иоанн Влах (Валах), Румынский, мч.» — so nothing was added to the life but a sentence saying what the Russian prints. The day page carries hymns for four of the saints it heads and nothing under his name. `dates` were not touched: the folder already carries 1662 off doxologia's own sentence. azbyka.ru was not read.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 12 mai — «Sfântul Mucenic Ioan Valahul»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 12ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Ιωάννης ο Βλάχος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 12 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same civil day the Romanian calendar already keeps him on, and it is plainly the same man: born in Wallachia, seized at fifteen by Tatars, hanged at Constantinople on 12 May 1662. **He is not the day's other John**: saint.gr keeps on this same 12 May a John the Neomartyr of Serres, a rich man's son burnt there about 1480, who is a new folder in batch `el-05-12`. **The Greek adds the manner and the circumstance the corpus may not hold**: the sultan Mehmed, the Tatar raid into Wallachia sent to put down the rising of the lord Michael the Voivode, the soldier he killed trying to escape, the widow of that soldier into whose hands he was given at Constantinople, the vizier's interrogation, the prefect's sentence, the hanging at Parmak Kapi, and the ransoming and burial of his body by Christians three days later. **The page names his passion's author**, John Karyophylles, and prints no hymn.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue at pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (20 September 2026).

hymns.text: Astăzi duhovniceşte prăznuieşte Biserica dreptcredincioşilor, şi cu bucurie strigă: Veniţi, iubitorilor de mucenici, să prăznuim pomenirea cea de peste an a luptelor noului mucenic Ioan! Că acesta, dintre noi cu voia lui Dumnezeu răsărind, în împărăteasca cetate a lui Constantin a înflorit minunat, aducând Stăpânului rod bogat şi bine primit, prin mucenicie. Iar acum se roagă neîncetat în ceruri, să se mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfântului Mucenic Ioan Valahul», Glasul 4

english.text: Today the Church of the Orthodox keeps spiritual feast, and cries out with joy: come, lovers of the martyrs, let us keep the yearly memory of the struggles of the new martyr John! For he, springing up from among us by the will of God, flowered wonderfully in the imperial city of Constantine, and brought to the Master a rich and well-received fruit by his martyrdom. And now he prays without ceasing in the heavens, that our souls may be saved.
